title: Mark Zuckerberg Says AI's Biggest Danger Isn't Rogue Models. It's Too Much Power In One Place.
key_facts: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg released a 6,500-word manifesto on Monday, which the article dates to 5 Oct 2026.
He argues the bigger danger is one government, company or institution controlling powerful AI, not the models themselves.
He argues that any policy slowing American model releases, even by a month, adds significant risk while foreign models race ahead.
Meta plans to open the weights of a new model, Muse Glimmer, and of a version of Muse Spark 1.2 in the coming weeks (Axios reported).
Meta's independent board will be given authority to approve safety criteria for model releases.
Zuckerberg announced a $1 billion 'Future is for Everyone Fund' for US communities with Meta data centres.
quote_evidence: "I'm personally more worried about centralization than I am about any of the specific risks others are talking about," Zuckerberg told Axios in an interview ahead of the manifesto's release.
"Any policy that slows American model releases, even by a month, could add significant risk to American leadership while letting foreign models race ahead," Zuckerberg wrote.
why_it_matters_hint: A major AI company's chief argues against slowing releases, which bears on how AI rules and open models develop.
event_date: Mon 5 Oct 2026 (article says 'released Monday'; article dated 8 Oct)
